_schema._about: Content for /blog and the /blog/<slug> article template. Structure follows the reference news page: a full-height dark hero (background image, small mark, display h1, sub), then a sand-m section with a row of category filter pills and a 3-column card grid (image area, then 'DATE  Title' in one line with the date in black and the title in grey). The eight articles are hypjam's existing markdown files; they are NOT rewritten. British English on the index copy; the article bodies are rendered as written.
_schema.hero: {background:{kind, alt}, mark, h1, sub} - background.kind = 'video-still-blur': a darkened blurred frame from the hero video (no photography exists). mark is the small hook mark file centred above the h1, as the reference places its mark.
_schema.filters: [string] - the pill row; 'All' first and active by default. Filtering hides cards whose category does not match; no page reload.
_schema.articles: [{slug, href, title, title_sentence, description, category, date, date_label, reading_minutes, words, sections, links_used, art, body}] in index order (newest-first is moot: all share a month, so this is editorial order). title is the article's title in sentence case (the reference's register), used everywhere: the card, <title>, the article h1 and the link_map labels; title_sentence carries the same value. The markdown's own lowercase H1 is stripped (see render.strip). description is the file's 'meta:' line verbatim (use for the card sub-line and the meta description). date is ISO year-month; date_label is what the card prints where the reference prints 'MM/DD'. art is a line-drawn motif key for the card's image area (the page agent draws it as a 16:10 sand tile with a 1px monoline SVG). body is the absolute path of the markdown to render on the article page.
_schema.link_map: {path: {href, label}} - the article bodies contain [[link:PATH]] tokens. The renderer replaces each token with label; for /blog/ paths the label is that article's title (sentence case). /hire does not exist on this site; the bodies still contain [[link:/hire]] tokens, so the '/hire' key stays and maps to /book (the '/book' key is kept alongside it).
_schema.render: {strip, features, tables} - what the markdown renderer must handle. Article bodies use ##/### headings, paragraphs, **bold**, bullet lists, numbered lists, [[link:]] tokens and pipe tables (five of the eight).
_schema.article_page: {back:{label, href}, byline, related_count, cta:{h2, p, button:{label, href}}} - the article template: back link at top, h1 = title, byline line 'date_label · reading_minutes min read · category', the rendered body in a ~720px column, then related_count cards from the same or nearest category, then the CTA.
